title: The bottleneck might be the air in the room
summary: This blog post explores the correlation between indoor CO2 levels and cognitive performance, arguing that elevated carbon dioxide concentrations in poorly ventilated rooms can significantly impair decision-making abilities. The author presents research findings showing measurable cognitive decline at various CO2 levels and discusses practical implications for workspace design and productivity optimization.
problem_solved: Addresses the overlooked environmental factor of indoor air quality that may be limiting team productivity and decision quality in modern workspaces.
why_valuable: Provides actionable insights backed by research that could help organizations improve cognitive performance simply by optimizing ventilation and air quality in their facilities.
